## Welcome

-   **Quarto** is an open-source publishing system for notebooks, docs, and slides.
-   This deck shows **step-by-step basics** to get you productive quickly.

Notes: - Use <kbd>Left/Right</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> to navigate. - Press <kbd>?</kbd> during presentation for built-in hotkeys.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Install Quarto

1.  Download from <https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/>
2.  Install for your OS (Windows, macOS, Linux)
3.  Verify in terminal:

``` bash
quarto check
```

**Tip:** If you use R or Python, ensure they are installed and on PATH.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Create Your First Doc

-   Create a new file: `hello.qmd`
-   Add minimal YAML and content:

``` yaml
---
title: "Hello Quarto"
format: html
---

Hello, Quarto!
```

-   Render:

``` bash
quarto render hello.qmd
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Make Slides (Reveal.js)

-   Set `format: revealjs` in YAML:

``` yaml
---
title: "My Slides"
format: revealjs
---
```

-   Separate slides using `---` (horizontal) and `##` headings:

``` markdown
## Slide 1
Content here

---

## Slide 2
More content
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

-   Preview live:

``` bash
quarto preview my-slides.qmd
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Basic Markdown

-   Paragraphs and line breaks as usual
-   Lists:
    -   `-` for bullets
    -   `1.` for numbered lists
-   Emphasis: `*italics*`, `**bold**`
-   Links: `[text](https://example.com)`
-   Images: `![](path/to/img.png)`


## Equations in Markdown

Math in Quarto uses LaTeX/MathJax—just write math inline with `$ ... $` or display with `$$ ... $$`.

- **Inline math:** The average batch size is $\bar{b} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} b_i$.
- **Display math:**  
  
  $$
  \text{Dough Yield} = \alpha + \beta_1(\text{Flour}) + \beta_2(\text{Butter}) + \beta_3(\text{Sugar})
  $$
  

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Code Chunks

-   Run code with fenced blocks and language label:

```{r}
#| echo: fenced
# R code runs when rendering
summary(cars)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Can run other languages besides R (e.g., python)
```{python}
#| echo: fenced
# Python code runs when rendering
print("Hello from Python")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

-   Control execution with options, e.g. `echo`, `warning`, `message`:

```{r}
#| echo: fenced
#| warning: false
#| message: false
plot(pressure)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Figures & Tables

-   Plots from code are auto-captured
-   Can add captions and alt text

```{r cookie_map_code, include=FALSE}


# install.packages(c("plotly", "dplyr", "htmlwidgets", "stringr", "tibble")) # if needed
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)
library(htmlwidgets)
library(stringr)
library(tibble)

# ---- Data: Top Christmas cookie by state ----
cookies <- c(
  "Alabama" = "Oatmeal Peanut Butter",
  "Alaska" = "Sugar Cookies",
  "Arizona" = "Raspberry Thumbprint",
  "Arkansas" = "Danish Butter",
  "California" = "Buche de Noel",
  "Colorado" = "Cake Mix Christmas",
  "Connecticut" = "Italian Christmas Cookies",
  "Delaware" = "Italian Christmas Cookies",
  "District of Columbia" = "Christmas Crack Cookies",
  "Florida" = "Oatmeal Raisin Cookies",
  "Georgia" = "Brownie Cookies",
  "Hawaii" = "Chocolate Peppermint",
  "Idaho" = "Sugar Cookies",
  "Illinois" = "Christmas Sink",
  "Indiana" = "Shortbread Cookies",
  "Iowa" = "Chocolate Crinkle",
  "Kansas" = "Peanut Butter with Kisses",
  "Kentucky" = "Peanut Butter with Kisses",
  "Louisiana" = "Buche de Noel",
  "Maine" = "Gingerbread Cookies",
  "Maryland" = "Christmas Crack Cookies",
  "Massachusetts" = "Chocolate Peppermint Cookies",
  "Michigan" = "Christmas Wreath",
  "Minnesota" = "Christmas Wreath",
  "Mississippi" = "Christmas Tree Cookies",
  "Missouri" = "Kitchen Sink",
  "Montana" = "Chocolate Chip",
  "Nebraska" = "Christmas Wreath",
  "Nevada" = "Christmas Kitchen Sink",
  "New Hampshire" = "Gingerbread",
  "New Jersey" = "Italian Christmas Cookies",
  "New Mexico" = "Italian Christmas",
  "New York" = "Greek Christmas",
  "North Carolina" = "Chocolate Cookies",
  "North Dakota" = "Grinch Cookies",
  "Ohio" = "Peanut Butter Blossoms",
  "Oklahoma" = "Kitchen Sink Cookies",
  "Oregon" = "Gingerbread Cookies",
  "Pennsylvania" = "Italian Christmas Cookies",
  "Rhode Island" = "Italian Christmas Cookies",
  "South Carolina" = "Peanut Butter Thumbprint",
  "South Dakota" = "Cranberry Pistachio",
  "Tennessee" = "Buche de Noel",
  "Texas" = "Snowball",
  "Utah" = "Pistachio",
  "Vermont" = "Sugar",
  "Virginia" = "Molasses Cookies",
  "Washington" = "Snowball Cookies",
  "West Virginia" = "Snowball",
  "Wisconsin" = "Sugar Cookies",
  "Wyoming" = "Italian Christmas Cookies"
)

# State abbreviations (incl. DC)
state_abbrev <- c(
  "Alabama"="AL","Alaska"="AK","Arizona"="AZ","Arkansas"="AR","California"="CA",
  "Colorado"="CO","Connecticut"="CT","Delaware"="DE","District of Columbia"="DC",
  "Florida"="FL","Georgia"="GA","Hawaii"="HI","Idaho"="ID","Illinois"="IL",
  "Indiana"="IN","Iowa"="IA","Kansas"="KS","Kentucky"="KY","Louisiana"="LA",
  "Maine"="ME","Maryland"="MD","Massachusetts"="MA","Michigan"="MI","Minnesota"="MN",
  "Mississippi"="MS","Missouri"="MO","Montana"="MT","Nebraska"="NE","Nevada"="NV",
  "New Hampshire"="NH","New Jersey"="NJ","New Mexico"="NM","New York"="NY",
  "North Carolina"="NC","North Dakota"="ND","Ohio"="OH","Oklahoma"="OK","Oregon"="OR",
  "Pennsylvania"="PA","Rhode Island"="RI","South Carolina"="SC","South Dakota"="SD",
  "Tennessee"="TN","Texas"="TX","Utah"="UT","Vermont"="VT","Virginia"="VA",
  "Washington"="WA","West Virginia"="WV","Wisconsin"="WI","Wyoming"="WY"
)

# Build data frame
df <- tibble(
  state = names(cookies),
  cookie = unname(cookies),
  abbr   = state_abbrev[state]
)

# ---- Categorize cookies per your rules ----
# Normalize cookie strings for robust matching
normalize_cookie <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    str_to_lower() %>%
    str_replace_all("\\b(cookies?|christmas)\\b", "") %>%
    str_replace_all("[^a-z ]", " ") %>%    # remove punctuation
    str_squish()
}

df <- df %>%
  mutate(norm = normalize_cookie(cookie),
         category = case_when(
           # Classic
           str_detect(norm, "chocolate chip")     |
           str_detect(norm, "^sugar\\b")          |
           str_detect(norm, "danish butter")      |
           str_detect(norm, "shortbread")         |
           str_detect(norm, "oatmeal raisin")     ~ "Classic",

           # Chocolate
           str_detect(norm, "^chocolate$")        |
           str_detect(norm, "brownie")            |
           str_detect(norm, "chocolate crinkle")  |
           str_detect(norm, "chocolate peppermint")|
           str_detect(norm, "chocolate cookies?") ~ "Chocolate",

           # Fruity/Nutty
           str_detect(norm, "pistachio")                  |
           str_detect(norm, "raspberry thumbprint")       |
           str_detect(norm, "peanut butter with kisses")  |
           str_detect(norm, "cranberry pistachio")        |
           str_detect(norm, "peanut butter blossoms?")    |
           str_detect(norm, "oatmeal peanut butter")      |
           str_detect(norm, "peanut butter thumbprint")   ~ "Fruity/Nutty",

           # Other
           str_detect(norm, "kitchen sink")       |
           str_detect(norm, "molasses")           ~ "Other",

           # Festive: everything else
           TRUE ~ "Festive"
         ))

# Factor with a fixed order for categories
cat_levels <- c("Classic","Chocolate","Fruity/Nutty","Other","Festive")
df <- df %>%
  mutate(category_factor = factor(category, levels = cat_levels),
         category_id     = as.integer(category_factor))

# Hover text: show State + Cookie (as requested)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(hover = paste0(state, "<br>Cookie: ", cookie))

# ---- Festive holiday color palette ----
# Classic       -> Frost Silver
# Chocolate     -> Chocolate Brown
# Fruity/Nutty  -> Evergreen
# Other         -> Gold
# Festive       -> Holly Red
cat_colors <- c(
  "Classic"      = "#386641", # Holly Green
  "Chocolate"    = "#43291f", # Chocolate Brown
  "Fruity/Nutty" = "#a7c957", # Soft Green
  "Other"        = "#B0BEC5", # Frost Silver
  "Festive"      = "#bc4749"  # Soft Red
)

# Build a discrete segmented colorscale aligned to 5 categories
n <- length(cat_levels)
colorscale <- list()
for (i in seq_len(n)) {
  start <- (i - 1) / n
  end   <- i / n
  col   <- unname(cat_colors[cat_levels[i]])
  colorscale <- append(colorscale, list(list(start, col), list(end, col)))
}

# ---- Plot ----
p <- plot_geo(df) %>%
  add_trace(
    type = "choropleth",
    locations = ~abbr,
    locationmode = "USA-states",
    z = ~category_id,                # numeric id enables discrete colorscale
    zmin = 1, zmax = n,
    text = ~hover,
    hoverinfo = "text",
    colorscale = colorscale,
    showscale = TRUE,
    colorbar = list(
      title = "Category",
      tickmode = "array",
      tickvals = 1:n,
      ticktext = cat_levels
    )
  ) %>%
  layout(
    geo = list(
      scope = "usa",
      showlakes = TRUE,
      lakecolor = "rgba(255,255,255,0.3)"
    ),
    margin = list(l = 0, r = 0, t = 60, b = 0)
  )
```

## Tables
-   Can easily create tables from data frames (R/Python) or using markdown

```{r, table_cookie}

library(gt)

# Original recipe (volume)
ingredients <- tibble::tibble(
  Volume = c(
    "2 3/4 cups all-purpose flour",
    "1 teaspoon baking soda",
    "1/2 teaspoon baking powder",
    "1 cup unsalted butter (softened)",
    "1 1/2 cups white sugar",
    "1 egg",
    "1 teaspoon vanilla extract",
    "1/2 teaspoon almond extract (optional)",
    "3 tablespoons milk",
    "Sprinkles or colored sugar (optional)"
  ),
  Weight = c(
    "330 g",   # Flour (2.75 cups × 120 g)
    "",        # Baking soda
    "",        # Baking powder
    "227 g",   # Butter (1 cup)
    "300 g",   # Sugar (1.5 cups × 200 g)
    "", "", "", "", "" # Others remain blank
  )
)

# Create a nicely formatted table
ingredients %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Ingredients: Volume → Weight",
    subtitle = "Converted only for large volume items (cups)"
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    Volume = "Ingredient (Volume)",
    Weight = "Weight (g)"
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_text(weight = "bold", color = "#BE0000")
    ),
    locations = cells_column_labels(everything())
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = "medium",
    heading.align = "center"
  )


```

---

| Ingredient (Volume)                         | Weight (g) |
|--------------------------------------------|-----------:|
| **2 3/4 cups all-purpose flour**           | **330 g**  |

| **1 1/2 cups white sugar**                 | **300 g**  |

## Slide Layout Tips

-   **Fragments (incremental bullets):**

``` markdown
- Bullet 1
- Bullet 2 {.fragment}
- Bullet 3 {.fragment}
```

-   **Columns:**

``` markdown
::: columns
::: column
Left content
:::

::: column
Right content
:::
:::
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

-   **Speaker notes:** add `Notes:` after slide content.

## Theming & Appearance

-   Change theme via YAML:

``` yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    theme: [simple, dark]
    transition: fade
    slide-number: true
```

-   Add a CSS file:

``` yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    css: styles.css
```

## Cross-References & Citations

-   Add bibliography in YAML:

``` yaml
bibliography: references.bib
```

-   Cite in text: `@smith2020` → renders a citation
-   Cross-ref figures/tables with labels:

```{r}
#| label: fig-cars
plot(cars)
```

Refer to Figure @fig-cars.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Projects & Directories

-   Make a Quarto project (optional):

``` bash
quarto create-project myproj
```

-   Render entire project:

``` bash
quarto render
```

-   Use `_quarto.yml` for shared settings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Publish & Share

-   Export formats: `html`, `pdf`, `docx`, `pptx` (for docs), `revealjs` for slides
-   Publish to **Quarto Pub**:

``` bash
quarto publish quarto-pub my-slides.qmd
```

-   Or host on GitHub Pages/Netlify; render to a `_site` directory for websites.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## VS Code / RStudio Integration

-   **VS Code:** install *Quarto* extension → run buttons & preview
-   **RStudio 2022.07+:** built-in Quarto → New File ▶ Quarto Document/Presentation

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Troubleshooting

-   Run `quarto check` to confirm engines & versions
-   Use `freeze: auto` to cache outputs in projects
-   If code doesn’t run, verify kernels (R, Python) and libraries
-   Clear cache: delete `.quarto/` and re-render
